items.description: The file-stock form page is served at its route: rendering <App> in MemoryRouter with initialEntries set to the stock-filing path mounts the file-stock form without crashing
The file-stock form renders a SKU input carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="sku-input")
The file-stock form renders a location input carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="location-input")
The file-stock form renders a quantity input carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="quantity-input")
The file-stock form renders an inventory-code input carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="inventory-code-input")
The file-stock form renders a submit button carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="submit-button")
app/routes/ does not import the SQLAlchemy Session object or any DB session dependency
app/services/ does not perform any direct database persistence operation
app/services/ contains no SQLAlchemy ORM imports (no Session, declarative_base, Column, or engine reference)
app/routes/ contains no SQLAlchemy ORM imports (no Session, declarative_base, Column, or engine reference)
the application resolves its database connection exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable
a validation error response payload identifies the specific invalid field by name rather than a generic message

When a POST to the stock API is made with a uuid-suffixed unique SKU, a location, a quantity, and a combined inventory_code, the API returns a success response and the persisted record contains that SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code
the integration test suite establishes its database connection via DATABASE_URL pointing at a real branch database with no in-memory or mock driver active
inserting a stock_records row with a NULL sku value raises a NOT NULL constraint violation at the real-branch database level
inserting a stock_records row with a NULL location value raises a NOT NULL constraint violation at the real-branch database level
inserting a stock_records row with a NULL inventory_code value raises a NOT NULL constraint violation at the real-branch database level
inserting a stock_records row with a NULL quantity value raises a NOT NULL constraint violation at the real-branch database level
inserting a stock_records row with quantity = -1 raises the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint at the real-branch database level
the service layer raises a rejection error when a filed quantity is negative, before any database write is attempted
running alembic downgrade then alembic upgrade on the stock_records migration completes without error against the real-branch database
The retrieve-stock page is served at its route: rendering <App> in MemoryRouter with initialEntries set to the retrieve-stock path mounts the retrieve view without crashing
When the API returns a stock record, the retrieve view displays the quantity in an element carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="quantity-display")
When the API returns a stock record, the retrieve view displays the inventory_code in an element carrying its data-testid seam (data-testid="inventory-code-display")
When the stock API is queried for a SKU-and-location that was previously filed, it returns the exact quantity that was submitted at write time
When the stock API is queried for a SKU-and-location that was previously filed, it returns the exact combined inventory_code that was submitted at write time
the stock boundary endpoint returns a JSON response body with no server-rendered HTML
When the API resolves a repeat submit with a success response, the file-stock form does not render an error element (no element with data-testid="form-error" is present in the DOM)
When a second POST is made to the stock API for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair with updated values, the API returns a success response rather than an error
When a second POST is made to the stock API for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair, querying the API returns exactly one record for that pair
inserting a second stock_records row for an already-existing (sku, location) pair raises a unique constraint violation at the real-branch database level
two concurrent transactions filing the same (sku, location) pair result in exactly one row stored in stock_records
the created_at column value on a stock_records row is unchanged after an in-place upsert on the same (sku, location) pair
